cases.title: The Wind Changed
cases.presentation: Industrial fire with 18 casualties. Your treatment area is set up 150 m east of the plant. Twenty minutes in, a light breeze shifts and smoke begins drifting toward the treatment area. Two treatment staff start coughing.
cases.question: What now?
options: A: Hand out surgical masks and continue.
B: Relocate the treatment area upwind immediately, re-mark zones, and inform IC/Safety and Transport of the new loading point.
C: Close the windows of the ambulances.
D: Transport everyone at once to the nearest hospital.
cases.explanation: Zones move with the hazard. A treatment area in smoke creates new casualties among patients and staff. Relocate and re-communicate flow.
cases.clinicalPearl: Check the wind every 15 minutes — tie a strip of tape to an antenna.

cases.title: Gridlock
cases.presentation: At a stadium MCI, ambulances are driving in from three directions, parking wherever they can, and backing out past the green collection point. Two crews almost hit walking wounded.
cases.question: Best fix?
options: A: Ask crews to drive carefully.
B: Move the greens into ambulances.
C: Establish one staging area on a single approach, a defined loading zone at the treatment exit, and a one-way exit route — communicate it to all units.
cases.explanation: Flow design solves congestion: one way in from staging, load, one way out.
cases.clinicalPearl: Draw the flow on the hood of your rig, then put it on the radio.

cases.title: Second Bag
cases.presentation: Fifteen minutes after an explosion at a bus terminal, a police officer reports an unattended backpack 20 m from your casualty collection point.
cases.question: Your action?
options: A: Evacuate the CCP and staff beyond the stand-off distance using cover, avoid radio use near the device, notify IC/police — continue care at the new location.
B: Open the bag to check.
C: Ignore it — police will handle it.
D: Move the backpack away yourself.
cases.explanation: Assume a secondary device. Move people out of line-of-sight beyond the stand-off distance; let bomb technicians manage it.
cases.clinicalPearl: Time, distance, cover — for bombs as for radiation.
